mainContent.content: A UCL master's dissertation exploring an LLM-based roundtable discussion simulator that lets designers acquire diverse perspectives by simulating debates among AI agents with different backgrounds, personalities, and traits.

content.title: Project cover and installation space rendering
Complex simulation system architecture and stakeholder investigation framework

mainContent.content: Traditional stakeholder research struggles with fragmented data, cognitive overload, and difficulty synthesizing insights. This system applies AI-driven social simulations to service design and stakeholder engagement.

content.title: Oversaturated text, difficulty locating valuable content, and the need for quick intent visualization

mainContent.content: Designers face three core challenges: oversaturated text from conflicting viewpoints, difficulty locating valuable content within massive transcripts, and lack of tools for quick intent visualization in immersive environments.

content.title: System architecture: OneAgent, RoundTable, and their dynamic interactions

mainContent.content: The system creates a dynamic, cyclical process of user input, agent interaction, and system analysis. OneAgent acts as the brain for each simulated stakeholder with memory, propose, and vote functions. RoundTable manages the overall discussion flow.

content.title: Interface for choosing topics, adding agent memory, and configuring agents

mainContent.content: Users configure agents, control discussion flow, and zoom into specific aspects. A key feature is the ability to add to an agent's memory in real-time, significantly reducing cognitive load.

content.title: PCA-based embedding visualization for tracking agent stance and performance

mainContent.content: PCA reduces the dimensionality of textual content, showing how agents' topic connections and performance evolve. Users can track current-round stances and compare agent performance across rounds.

content.title: Vector distance tracking and 3D PCA visualization showing agent alignment

mainContent.content: Evaluation shows agents generally aligned with round topics. The 3D PCA visualization demonstrates tighter clustering of ideas and greater content alignment as the discussion progresses.

content.title: Study setup comparing traditional method with the system, questionnaire design, and participant demographics

mainContent.content: 6 participants (mean age 23.5) from diverse backgrounds — politics, architecture, UX, fashion, finance — compared the system against traditional methods through structured tasks and questionnaires.

content.title: Quantitative comparison: traditional method vs. our design across 15 metrics

mainContent.content: Quantitative results show significant improvements over the traditional method. Participants using the system completed tasks faster and gathered more insights, with strong improvements in trend identification and content analysis.

content.title: System limitations: lack of multi-modal LLMs and ethical considerations

mainContent.content: Current limitations include the lack of multi-modal LLMs, limited language-based representations of design challenges, and the need for real-world validation. Ethical considerations in simulating human stakeholders remain an open question.

content.title: Summary: simulating multi-stakeholder discussions and advanced visualization techniques

mainContent.content: Key contributions include simulating multi-stakeholder discussions using LLMs and advanced visualization techniques. The system enhances collaborative decision-making in design and planning processes while making stakeholder engagement more efficient and inclusive.

content.title: Future directions: enhanced agent complexity, multi-modal inputs, and policy development applications

mainContent.content: Future work aims to enhance agents' complexity and adaptability, explore multi-modal inputs for richer visual and spatial representation, and apply the system to other domains such as policy development.

This research reframes stakeholder engagement from a static data-collection exercise into a dynamic, interactive simulation. By combining LLM-based agent debates with dimensionality-reduced intent visualization, it transforms the way designers perceive and synthesize conflicting viewpoints. The core insight is that **multi-agent social simulation + spatial visualization = scalable stakeholder research** — reducing weeks of interviews into hours of guided simulation while maintaining depth and nuance. The limitation lies in language-only representation; integrating multi-modal perception will be the next frontier.
